Military Police in Água Clara received a tip that a man was selling drugs from a
white VW Gol in the Jardim das Palmeiras neighbourhood. The operation took
place on Wednesday 4 November 2026. The driver fled when he saw the patrol
car and was caught after a chase of several blocks. Officers found a
portion of a substance resembling cocaine in the car.

At the suspect's home, police seized portions of marijuana, a precision scale,
packaging material and money. A task force of Military Police and Civil
Police then found two other people involved at a snack bar. The teams found
59 tabletes, or blocks, of a substance resembling marijuana, totalling about 54
kilograms. Information gathered during the operation led the teams to a
drug hideout in a wooded area near the MS-324.

The suspect and the two other people were taken to the Civil Police station in
Água Clara for legal procedures.

report.body:
Officers of the Mossos d'Esquadra's criminal investigation division (DIC)
arrested seven men aged between 29 and 55 on 1 October 2026 on suspicion of
belonging to a drug-trafficking organisation. The operation took place at
an industrial warehouse in Cabanes, in the Alt Empordà district of Girona, where
officers seized 8,025 kg of hashish. The Mossos said the warehouse was used
only to store and distribute drugs.

Inside the trailer, officers found the hashish hidden among the merchandise in
pallets, packed in large raffia sacks filled with rubber crumbs, a method the
force said is used to make detection harder at police and customs checks.
The Mossos valued the haul at more than 16.2 million euros on the illicit
market. The force said the seizure amounted to 53.9% of the 14.9 tonnes of
hashish it had seized in 2026 by 1 October and was among the most significant
operations in its history.

The investigation began in June 2026, when officers in Viladecans, Barcelona,
stopped a van carrying nearly 2,400 kg of hashish and the Gavà court took the
case. On the day of the raid, officers saw people replace the vehicles'
number plates with others fixed by zip ties before the trailer was driven into
the warehouse and its door closed. Inside, they found seven people
unloading pallets of hashish to load into several vans for distribution.
Officers also found a firearm in one of the detainees' vans. Mossos
d'Esquadra video distributed by Europa Press TV shows the arrests at the
warehouse.

The seven detainees were handed to the Civil and Instruction Section of the
Tribunal de Instancia in Figueres. The investigation remains open and
further arrests have not been ruled out.

report.title: Driver arrested in Ceuta port as 300 kg hashish found in truck
report.summary: Spain's UDYCO drug unit arrested a truck driver at the port of Ceuta after finding a hidden compartment packed with bags of hashish, and a court ordered him held in preventive detention two days later. Outlets estimate the haul at about 300 kilograms, pending an official weighing.
report.body:
Spain's UDYCO drug unit arrested a truck driver at the port of Ceuta carrying a
stash of hashish hidden in a sophisticated false bottom. The driver was arrested at the port on Friday 13 November. Officers
intercepted the truck on the port road at the Muelle de Poniente and searched it
with support from the UPR prevention unit and the canine group. They found
the hashish and detained the driver, showing him the drugs found in the vehicle
he was driving.

The truck appeared empty and was heading toward boarding for Spain when a
specialist drugs dog alerted, prompting an exhaustive hours-long search inside
and outside the vehicle. After the hours-long detailed inspection, officers
found a large number of bags full of hashish inside the truck's structure.
Officers recovered numerous bags of hashish from the trailer's false bottom,
with first estimates putting the haul above 300 kilograms although police gave
no official weight. Officers used hammers, shears, mallets and an angle grinder to break open the protective sheet metal of the false bottom. The submitted account describes the seizure as about
300 kilograms of hashish arriving from Morocco.

The handcuffed driver was taken to police headquarters and placed under
investigation for an offence against public health. A court ordered the truck driver held in preventive detention after he was brought before it on Sunday 15 November on an offence against public health. Police link the
operation to open UDYCO investigations into groups moving hashish from Ceuta to
mainland Spain in heavy vehicles with hidden compartments. The investigation remained open on suspicion of larger consignments and of heavy vehicles being kept in premises used as hashish stash houses.

report.body:
Officers of the National Police's Drugs and Organised Crime Unit (Udyco)
arrested at least three people on Mallorca who were storing almost 50 kilos of
hashish for sale. In all, officers seized 60 kilos of hashish, the force said. The National Police later put the operation at five arrests, four men and one woman suspected of drug trafficking and membership of a criminal group. The suspects received the hashish from the Spanish
mainland in courier parcels, according to the newspaper's case sources. Officers intercepted a parcel containing 24 kilos of hashish addressed to a man living in Palma and arrested him on suspicion of drug trafficking. The
arrests took place on Wednesday 4 November. Officers searched a home in
Marratxí, a municipality east of Palma, and another in a town in es Raiguer, the
district around the town of Inca. An investigating court in Palma declared
the case secret. Investigators had followed the suspects for some time;
over the previous months they had collected parcels of the drug from courier
companies and kept them at home for sale through others in the network.

In the Marratxí search, police found a large quantity of hashish in a chest
freezer and an air rifle. In the main suspect's home, officers found 36 kilos of hashish, about 10,000 euros in cash and a compressed-air rifle with a silencer, and arrested the man and a woman on suspicion of drug trafficking and membership of a criminal group. A woman was arrested there over her alleged link
to the criminal organisation and was released at the police station hours later. Two more people were arrested the same day, and all the suspects are
Spanish nationals. A further person was arrested in connection with the case. In the second home, officers arrested a second suspect, who allegedly stored and transported drugs, and seized two kilos of cocaine, further doses and cutting agent, a 9 mm pistol, a bow with arrows and a hydraulic press.

The investigation is still open, further arrests are not ruled out, and the
suspects were due to appear before a Palma court in the coming hours. Officers from the Prevention and Reaction Unit, Group II of the anti-drug squad and the dog unit took part in the searches.

report.body:
Immigration police and Department of Thai Traditional and Alternative Medicine
officials searched a rented luxury house in Soi Khu Bon 27, Yaek 14, Tha Raeng
subdistrict, Bang Khen district, Bangkok, at 1pm on 19 October 2026.
Officers found one Vietnamese national and four Myanmar nationals sorting
cannabis buds inside the house. They seized more than five tonnes of
cannabis buds packed in black bags across all three floors. The four
Myanmar workers were paid 200 to 300 baht a day to sort and pack the buds.

Neighbours had complained about a strong cannabis smell from the house before
the raid. Police said they spent about two months gathering evidence after
the complaints. The three-storey house covered about 100 square wah and had
ventilation ducts installed to carry the smell outside. A Thai national
signed the lease, and the foreigners had lived and worked there for more than a
year. Police said the Vietnamese man appeared to be supervising the
operation, which was run like a company.

On-anong Srisuwan, a legal affairs official at the Department of Thai
Traditional and Alternative Medicine, said the group held a licence to process
cannabis buds in Nong Bua Lam Phu province that did not cover Bangkok. She
said the offence carried a maximum penalty of one year in prison and/or a fine
of 20,000 baht. The seized buds were to be sent to a laboratory to
establish whether they were grown in Thailand or imported. The suspects
were in custody while police pursued further investigation and legal action. Police said they were tracing the source of the cannabis and all involved
parties.

report.body:
Mehmet Arıcan, a construction worker, disappeared in Taşpınar Mahallesi in
Mustafakemalpaşa, Bursa, on 7 September 2010. His body was found four days
later at Karanlıkdere in the forest, and he had been shot dead with a hunting
rifle. Three suspects were detained at the time, but no prosecution
followed and the file was put on permanent search.

Sixteen years later, the Mustafakemalpaşa chief public prosecutor's office
re-examined phone records, financial inquiries and new witness statements.
JASAT, the gendarmerie's crime investigation team, raided eight addresses
simultaneously on 11 November 2026. Officers detained 17 suspects in the
raids. A court remanded one of them, H.F., in custody, and the other 16
were released.

The investigation concluded that the killing resulted from a feud over entering
a cannabis field without permission. At the time of the killing, Arıcan and
H.F. were in that feud.

The Inhulskyi District Court in Mykolaiv sentenced a local man to nine years in
prison for growing cannabis on his household plot and storing it for sale.
The man was 51 and had grown the cannabis since April 2026, according to the
prosecution. Police detained him in summer 2026 and notified him of
suspicion. Police searched the property on 25 July 2026. Officers
seized 14 cannabis plants and more than 8 kilograms of cannabis stored in the
attic. The police statement said officers found more than 10 kilograms of
dried raw material. He dried part of the harvest in the attic and ground
and packed the rest in glass jars for storage and, according to investigators,
sale.

He was charged under Part 3 of Article 307 of the Criminal Code, illegal
manufacture and storage of narcotics for sale on an especially large scale, and
Part 1 of Article 310, illegal sowing or growing of cannabis. He admitted
growing the plants but said he made the cannabis only for his own use and did
not intend to sell it. The court called that an attempt to avoid criminal
responsibility. It noted that he had previously served five years in prison
for growing cannabis. It sentenced him to nine years without confiscation
of property. It ordered the plants and cannabis destroyed. It also
ordered him to pay 28,400 hryvnias for expert examinations.

The 133,120 hryvnias bail paid for him is to be returned to his brother once the
verdict takes effect. The verdict has not entered into force. It can
be appealed to the Mykolaiv Court of Appeal within 30 days.
